title: Pacing Heuristic Quant Probe - Lab Journal (Oct 2026)
content:
Summary:

This is a lab journal for an exploratory sweep of request pacing heuristics aimed at reducing kernel churn and tail latency for quantized (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) models on our serving runtime. The idea: small, short-lived bursts of requests are causing frequent kernel rebinds and cache thrash on GPUs when switching between kernels (dense vs mixed-precision kernels). We hypothesize that a lightweight pacing layer between request ingress and the scheduler can smooth arrival patterns and reduce kernel switching overhead without significantly impacting median latency or throughput.

Motivation / Observed problem:
- On mixed workloads (short chat + long generation), we observe periods of high kernel-switch frequency. Sample trace: frequent toggles between AWQ-int8 kernels and FP8 fallback kernels across 100-ms windows.
- Kernel switch penalty measured (instrumentation): ~1.1-2.4 ms per switch on A100 gen2 with our current dispatcher (depends on kernel flavor and memory rebind). During 95th/99th percentile bursts this accumulates into +15-40 ms tail latency.
- Batching and static throttles reduce throughput or increase cold-start miss rate. Need a lightweight dynamic approach that adapts pacing per-model and per-kernel-family.

Experiment goal:
1) Build a tiny pacing shim that can: accept requests, FIFO buffer up to N ms/requests, and release at configurable pacing intervals (ms between release slices).
2) Evaluate across kernels: INT8-AWQ, INT8-GPTQ, FP8-accelerated kernel, and our dense FP16 baseline.
3) Measure median/95/99 latencies, token/sec, kernel-switch count, and percent time spent in kernel load/unload.
4) Test impact on quality metrics for AWQ/GPTQ (perplexity drift and 100-sample LM eval) to ensure pacing doesn't change model outputs.

Workload and test harness:
- Traffic generator: replay traces from customer-sim corpus (chatty, long-gen, mixed). Configs: small-chat (avg 2 turns, 80 tokens), long-gen (avg 1 turn, 1024 tokens), mixed (50/50).
- Hardware: A100-80GB (single-GPU), H100-80GB (sanity), local dev GPU (A10).
- Models: rdlw/llama2-13b-int8-awq (AWQ), rdlw/llama2-13b-gptq (GPTQ), rdlw/llama2-13b-fp8 (FP8 build), rdlw/llama2-13b-fp16 (baseline).
- Instrumentation: per-request timeline via tracing (trace id), per-kernel binding events (timestamped), CUDA event timings for kernel load/unload, and runtime counters for KV cache hits.

Pacing shim design (prototype):
- Queue: lock-free ring buffer per model routed on request signature (model+route).
- Policy: fixed slice pacing (release X requests every Y ms) + adaptive backoff when kernel-switch rate > threshold T.
- Low overhead path: shim in runtime IO thread, decision point before scheduler enqueue. We intentionally avoided deep async work to keep latency predictable.

Key configs tried:
- slice_size = [1, 4, 8]
- slice_interval_ms = [2, 5, 10, 20]
- backoff_threshold_switches_per_sec = [50, 150, 500]
- max_buffer_ms = [25, 100]

Preliminary results (single-GPU, mixed workload):
- Baseline (no pacing): median token latency = 9.7 ms, p95 = 45.3 ms, p99 = 114.1 ms, kernel-switches/sec = 620, kernel-load-time% = 12.9%
- slice_size=4, interval=5ms: median = 10.4 ms (+7%), p95 = 32.8 ms (-28%), p99 = 68.4 ms (-40%), kernel-switches/sec = 210 (-66%), kernel-load-time% = 5.2%
- slice_size=8, interval=10ms: median = 12.1 ms (+25%), p95 = 29.9 ms (-34%), p99 = 66.2 ms (-42%), kernel-switches/sec = 190 (-69%), kernel-load-time% = 4.7%
- slice_size=1, interval=2ms: median approx baseline, p95 ~42ms, p99 ~102ms; tiny improvements only.

Interpretation:
- Smoothing arrivals reduces kernel churn significantly and cuts tail latency by ~35-45% for mixed workloads. Median latency increases modestly depending on slice size/interval. There is a clear Pareto tradeoff between median and tail.
- Larger slice_size and interval produce fewer kernel switches but increase median. slice_size=4 / interval=5ms looks like a sweet spot in these traces.
- Kernel-load-time% correlates with switch rate; pacing reduces this and frees GPU cycles for token generation vs rebinds.

Per-kernel observations:
- AWQ-int8: shows the largest benefit from pacing. The AWQ kernel has a higher per-switch setup cost due to extra weight unpack/packing steps; reducing switches yields large gains.
- GPTQ-int8: gains present but smaller (kernel is leaner).
- FP8 kernel: modest improvements; sometimes pacing nudges the scheduler into larger batch formation (beneficial) but on very long requests adds overhead.
- FP16 baseline: least affected (it is already stable and cold-start optimized).

Quality checks (sanity):
- Ran LM-eval subset of 100 prompts before/after pacing; AWQ/GPTQ output metrics (simple per-token logprob mean) unchanged within noise: delta < 0.04 nats on average.
- Determinism: no reordering of requests, FIFO preserved.

Edge cases / regressions spotted:
- Under extreme sustained throughput close to saturation, pacing increases queueing and can push the GPU to steady-state backpressure; throughput drops if max_buffer_ms is too small. Need to adapt max buffer to QPS.
- Multi-model node: when models with very different kernel families co-reside, per-model pacing helps but global pacing (cross-model) is needed for fairness.
- Cold path: for low QPS (< 3 rps per model) the shim adds noise; we need a bypass for low-util models.

Instrumentation snippets (examples):
- kernel switch event log (shortened):
  [2026-10-08T15:12:22.312Z] trace=abc123 model=llama2-13b-awq kernel=AWQ_int8 bind_start=0.013ms bind_end=1.247ms
  [2026-10-08T15:12:22.319Z] trace=abc124 model=llama2-13b-fp8 kernel=FP8 bind_start=0.014ms bind_end=0.432ms

- example perf counter output (condensed):
  kernel_switches: 210/s
  avg_bind_latency: 0.86 ms
  kernel_load_time_ratio: 5.2%

Open questions / follow-ups:
1) Can we make the pacing fully adaptive to observed kernel switch rate while guaranteeing an upper bound on added median latency per SLO? (PID-style controller?)
2) How to integrate with existing batching heuristics so pacing complements, not conflicts, with dynamic batch formation?
3) Should pacing be a node-global module (help when multi-model interference happens) or per-model only? Tradeoffs: global can be more optimal but needs cross-model admission control and fairness knobs.
4) Can we detect kernel-family affinity of incoming requests earlier (signature-based) to route similar-flavor requests to the same micro-slice to further reduce switches?
5) How does pacing interact with Dedicated pools and autoscaling? We need to ensure autoscaler signals don't maddeningly flip due to transient pacing-induced queueing.

Next steps / proposed plan:
- Short (1-week): harden shim implementation, add bypass for low QPS, add adaptive backoff loop with simple exponential smoothing. Run full sweep across A100/H100 and add more customer-sim traces.
- Medium (2-4 weeks): integrate pacing into the edge dispatcher as an optional per-model flag, create a metric dashboard (kernel-switch-rate, avg_bind_latency, pacing_buffer_ms), and add rollout canary. Add unit/integration tests that assert no request reordering.
- Long (6-10 weeks): prototype global admission controller aware of kernel families, explore integration with Optimize recommendations (automatically suggest pacing for heavy-switch models), evaluate on Dedicated customer traces and adjust defaults.

Notes to self (quick checklist):
- Add param to runtime config: pacing.enabled, pacing.slice_size, pacing.slice_interval_ms, pacing.max_buffer_ms
- Put a guard: if current_p95_latency < baseline_p95 * 1.05 then disable pacing automatically (avoid regressions)
- Add an e2e regression harness that runs a 10-min mixed trace and flags tail latency increase > 10%

Attachments referenced:
- JIRA-RT-8721: trace bundles and raw perf counters (point to storage)
- PR #4512: initial shim implementation (WIP)

If anyone wants to run these experiments locally: contact me (Asha) and I will share the traffic corpus + small helper script.

-- end of journal entry (oct 2026)
